first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state battery. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The LATP and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 83% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 60 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.9 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 1000 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF, Li3YCl6, and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 250 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. A precursor of the LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 4.2 mS/cm. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder for lithium battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and a porosity of 16% or less is provided. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability and interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and Li2ZrO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 90%. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A wet film of an ion-conductive solid cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The binder content of 2 wt% to 10 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 45 wt% to 90 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 250 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 140 degrees C.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on phosphate-based NASICON and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Solid electrolyte oxygen sensor element with a heater and protective layer
abstract: An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting carbon dioxide comprises a sodium beta-alumina ceramic, a sensing electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite, and a reference electrode exposed to a reference gas. The sensing electrode comprises lanthanum strontium manganite and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. The sensor detects carbon dioxide with high selectivity and a response time of 5 seconds. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The limiting current is proportional to the carbon dioxide concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The sensor operating at 500 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for carbon dioxide.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising sodium nitrite in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects carbon dioxide.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 150 degrees C. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. A precursor of the LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. The LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with monoclinic structure and method for producing the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 7.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and production method thereof
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The LLTO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Part of the titanium in the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 83% or more.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiTaO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF). A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and LiF material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Gallium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.16 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 3 mol% to 23 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1030 degrees C to 1380 degrees C.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF). A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The bilayer structure improves the cycle life compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 40 nm to 200 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state battery. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with aluminum and sintered with Li2CO3 is described. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LATP, LLTO, and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The grain size is 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 92% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 2 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 80% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sheet formability. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The solid content is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an oxygen-rich surface region is described. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved cycle life and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an oxygen substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The LGPS and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.045 or less. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less.

title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance and dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). The lithium fluoride additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5% after 100 cycles. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1.
