abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A sheet of 20 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. In the monoclinic structure, indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an oxygen-rich surface region is described. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from acetonitrile, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li7P3S11 phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing GeS2. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The Li3PS4, LATP, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C has a thickness of 15 micrometers. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ceramic ion conductor, and the layer shows improved sheet formability and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with trigonal structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state battery. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobium tantalum oxide formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The LiNbO3 and Li2ZrO3 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. The dopant tantalum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The grain size is 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and the relative density is 93% or more after sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The additive content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, the stack pressure is 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and the critical current density is 1 mA/cm2. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state lithium battery. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with an indium additive. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The indium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The cell shows no short circuit for 300 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the electronic conductivity of the ion-conductive solid layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.8% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.35 <= y/a <= 0.65.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium scandium chloride ion-conductive solid with monoclinic structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which hafnium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium chloride framework. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.02 to 0.25. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The resulting LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium erbium chloride ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 8.5 mS/cm. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.075 or less. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.12 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which titanium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. The solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium zirconate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The Li6PS5Cl, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 80% or more.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with a zinc additive. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 and Li3PS4 material. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The critical current density is 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.2% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Potentiometric ammonia sensor having an auxiliary electrode of barium carbonate
abstract: An exhaust gas sensor with a pumping cell, a sensing cell, and a diffusion controlling portion is described. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux. A solid electrolyte based sensor does not require a liquid electrolyte and operates at high temperature. The ammonia sensor can be used for combustion control and emission monitoring at 300 degrees C. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the lanthanum strontium manganite sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The protective layer improves the durability of the yttria-stabilized zirconia sensor in an exhaust gas. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 300 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting ammonia, comprising: a ceramic body comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia; a sensing electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 300 degrees C.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a silicon substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The Li7P3S11 and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.6 wt% or less.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which zinc is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium fluoride (LiF). A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and the critical current density is 4 mA/cm2. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 60 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 0.4 MPa to 10 MPa.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium zirconate and to a method for producing the same. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3 and Li6PS5Cl material. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The oxide particles have a core of the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. With germanium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ion-conductive solid. The protective layer thickness is 20 nm to 100 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.3% or more. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The low electronic conductivity of the LiF and Li3YCl6 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 5 nm to 300 nm.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 20 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The additive comprises zinc in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved dendrite suppression and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more.

assignee_std: CORAST INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The LLZO, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The oxygen substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours is 65% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A solid electrolyte sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state lithium battery including the sheet are described. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 16% or less, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an oxygen substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a tin substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air for lithium battery
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3YCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium yttrium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

assignee_std: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A precursor of the Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An ionic conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.8.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. The LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery.
