The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state lithium battery using it. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The material comprises Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of Li2O is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The tin substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A precursor of the LLZO and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a tin substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP, Li3PS4, and LLZO material. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 84% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by sputtering. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. The LiPON layer of 300 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 30 nm to 1800 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3InCl6. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The resulting Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the electrochemical window of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 40 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2 mS/cm or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by cold isostatic pressing
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film without any solvent. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The sheet thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, the porosity is 20% or less, and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 250 micrometers, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.15 MPa or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 40% or less.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The solid electrolyte provides improved ionic conductivity and cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.25 <= x <= 1.05.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing silica nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm are obtained. The anion is covalently bonded to the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The 50 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium hexafluorophosphate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 65% or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl propionate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. The oxygen substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and beta-Li3PS4. A precursor of the LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 4.2 mS/cm. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.2 <= y/a <= 0.5.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with an indium additive. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Specific examples are Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, the porosity is 16% or less, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The LiF and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a ceramic ion conductor layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state battery. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 1200 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7P3S11. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein 0.2 <= y/a <= 0.5, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% after 100 cycles. The LLZO, Li3YCl6, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life and dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant niobium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 96% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent anisole. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 30 micrometers. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.5 wt% to 25 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and ZrBr4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state lithium battery. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The GeS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3InCl6. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The low electronic conductivity of the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3InCl6, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The Li3InCl6, Li6PS5Cl, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The material comprises Li3InCl6, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and production method thereof
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with tantalum and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sintered body has a relative density of 95%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.05 <= v <= 0.4, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 92% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 2 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by solution casting followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The Ag-C layer of 100 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The LGPS and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55.

title: Conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and capacitor using the same
abstract: Described is a solid electrolytic capacitor element whose leakage current is reduced by a repair step of the dielectric film. The polyaniline is doped with polystyrene sulfonate and has a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm in the dispersion. The hybrid structure improves the self-healing of the dielectric film on the niobium anode. The polystyrene sulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 105 degrees C storage. A re-formation step after polymer formation repairs defects in the dielectric film and reduces the leakage current. The capacitor withstands 105 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor comprising a plurality of capacitor elements stacked and electrically connected in parallel, each capacitor element comprising a niobium anode body, a dielectric layer, and a conductive polymer layer, and a resin encapsulation, wherein the capacitor has a rated voltage of 10 V.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.05 <= y/a <= 0.55.

title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising an Ag-C inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by thermal evaporation followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The Li3N layer of 50 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved dendrite suppression and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. A precursor of the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 5.5 mS/cm. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6. The Li3InCl6 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The average thickness of the coating is 4 nm to 20 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 material. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent.
