abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 4.5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 85%. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity and sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. A precursor of the LiF, Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The LiF, Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and the critical current density is 2 mA/cm2. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.55.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.15 to 0.5, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 0 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF). An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The LiF material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising an Ag-C inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF material. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state lithium battery. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 0.2 micrometers to 12 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The solvent is acetonitrile, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air for lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The arsenic-free antimony content of 1 mol% to 4 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 0.7 mS/cm or more. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The oxygen substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the dendrite suppression is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.2% or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mA/cm2 or more.

assignee_std: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Zirconium-substituted lithium indium chloride ion-conductive ceramic with a trigonal close-packed anion lattice and oxidation-stable lithium cell
abstract: An ion-conductive ceramic for a lithium cell has a composition represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.4, and a trigonal crystal phase in which chloride anions form a close-packed sublattice and indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites. The zirconium substitution introduces lithium vacancies, and the cation disorder between the lithium site and the metal site is 10% or more, which lowers the activation energy for lithium migration to 0.33 eV or less. The ceramic is prepared by mixing LiCl, InCl3, and ZrCl4 in a sealed container, mechanochemically reacting the mixture, and heat-treating the reacted powder at 250 degrees C to 320 degrees C under argon; alternatively the chloride is crystallized from an aqueous solution and dehydrated under vacuum at 200 degrees C. The ceramic has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and is stable against oxidation up to 4.4 V versus Li/Li+, so that it can be mixed directly with an uncoated layered oxide positive electrode material. A lithium cell in which the positive electrode mixture contains the ceramic and the separator layer contains a sulfide glass ceramic or lithium fluoride-containing composite shows a widened electrochemical window and stable cycling at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. An ion-conductive ceramic comprising a crystal phase of a lithium indium zirconium chloride represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.4, the crystal phase being trigonal and having a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein a cation disorder between a lithium site and a metal site determined by Rietveld refinement is 10% or more, and wherein the ion-conductive ceramic has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 32 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The content of LiI is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of LiI is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity of the all-solid-state lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell operable at 650 to 800 degrees C and fuel cell system
abstract: A reversible solid oxide cell with a 5 micrometer electrolyte operable in fuel cell mode and electrolysis mode at 650 to 800 degrees C is described. The solid electrolyte layer of gadolinium-doped ceria conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. The stack shows stable operation over 200 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 650 to 800 degrees C. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 650 to 800 degrees C. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode at 650 to 800 degrees C. The thin 5 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.0 W/cm2. The cell operates at 650 to 800 degrees C with a power density of 1.0 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 200 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising gadolinium-doped ceria, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 5 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on the barrier layer.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The tin substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the grain boundary resistance are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 70% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium erbium bromide ion-conductive solid with monoclinic structure
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.02 to 0.25. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C.

title: Germanium-substituted NASICON-type LATP ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 5.2 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more and a conductivity of 0.35 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming a solid electrolyte layer. The viscosity of 500 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. An all-solid-state battery using the layer shows improved interfacial resistance and a thin electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The Li6PS5Cl, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.15 or less. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more during cycling is described. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 100 MPa. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a beta-Li3PS4 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The Li3PS4 and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3PS4 and LGPS material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of Li2O is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering an aluminum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 89% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1200 degrees C, and the resulting density is 92%. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 84% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1000 degrees C to 1350 degrees C, and wherein 0.31 <= v <= 1.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The dopant gallium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The sintered body has a relative density of 92%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.42 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 89% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a lithium secondary battery including the sheet are described. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers after calendering. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The method shortens the process and improves the ionic conductivity and sheet formability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 200 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with tantalum and sintered with LiF is described. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 96% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The Li6PS5Cl, LATP, and Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7P3S11. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.05 <= v <= 0.4.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, LiNbO3, and Li2ZrO3 material. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which zirconium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A solid-state battery comprising the LGPS and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6, and wherein 0.2 <= y/a <= 0.5, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 35 wt% to 80 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 50 mPa s to 2500 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with aluminum and sintered with Al2O3 is described. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.1 to 0.45, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The total ionic conductivity is 0.28 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1000 degrees C to 1350 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 89% or more, and wherein 0.06 <= v <= 0.75.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and a porosity of 16% or less is provided. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sheet of 20 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 16% or less, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1.
