A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing LiI. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Hafnium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO solid electrolyte stable above 4.5 V and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The oxidation potential is 4.5 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity and sinterability in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 3.9 V or more.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium erbium bromide ceramic ion conductor with orthorhombic structure and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which titanium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium bromide framework. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the content of Li2O is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 40 nm to 200 nm.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 80 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 15 micrometers. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. With zirconium substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 73% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The dopant gallium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 91% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The binder content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 60 degrees C to form a continuous film. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.3 MPa or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3YCl6. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C has a thickness of 50 micrometers. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF, LLZO, and Li3YCl6 material. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 20 degrees C to 120 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 420 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with an indium additive. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1.5 mA/cm2. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more, and wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved sheet formability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.8 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition for lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 2 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the sinterability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.9 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An ionic conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.2 to 1.6. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.55.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium indium chloride and to a method for producing the same. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with niobium and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LATP and LLTO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. When v is 0.5, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The viscosity of 3000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the sheet formability and cycle life of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state lithium battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y). An ionic conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.3 to 1.7. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.75, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 420 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor element with a polyaniline layer and a carbon cathode layer
abstract: Provided is a multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor in which capacitor elements are stacked and connected in parallel. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion. The capacitor has a capacitance of 330 microfarads, a rated voltage of 35 V, and an equivalent series resistance of 8 milliohms at 100 kHz. The polyaniline layer lowers the equivalent series resistance to 8 milliohms compared with manganese dioxide. The capacitor rated at 35 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage. A solid electrolyte of polyaniline replaces the liquid electrolyte of a conventional electrolytic capacitor. A re-formation step after polymer formation repairs defects in the dielectric film and reduces the leakage current.
first_claim: 1. A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising polyaniline particles doped with polystyrene sulfonate, a polyhydric alcohol, and water, wherein the particles have a median diameter of 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 45% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%.

title: Germanium-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved moisture stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using 1,2-dimethoxyethane
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS material. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of Li2O is 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.15 or less. A precursor of the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm and a relative density of 95%. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.11 <= v <= 0.8, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1030 degrees C to 1380 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO, Li3PS4, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. With the additive in an amount of 1 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3%. The additive comprises zinc in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The zinc additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which indium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% to suppress dendrites. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5% after 100 cycles. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3InCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1.
