The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 8.5 mS/cm. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state battery. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium scandium chloride ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure for lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 30% or less, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A solid-state lithium battery using the sheet shows improved sheet formability and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3BO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li2ZrO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by sputtering for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. The bilayer structure improves the cycle life compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LGPS material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The GeS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. The Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and polyvinylidene fluoride binder
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, ketjen black, and polyvinylidene fluoride is described. The cathode delivering 1000 mAh/g is assembled into a lithium battery with a lithium metal foil. The ketjen black framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of nickel sulfide. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The carbon coating on the nickel sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 80% at 25 degrees C. The active material nickel sulfide is combined with ketjen black and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The nickel sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising nickel sulfide, ketjen black, and polyvinylidene fluoride, wherein a loading of the nickel sulfide is 4 mg/cm2 or more.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 420 degrees C.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in 1,2-dimethoxyethane at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3YCl6 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The resulting Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6. The protective layer thickness is 80 nm to 400 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: A method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The viscosity of 500 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. A lithium secondary battery using the layer shows improved cycle life and a thin electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 50 mPa s to 2500 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 80 degrees C to 180 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a zinc-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. With the additive in an amount of 1 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7%. The zinc additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using acetonitrile and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from acetonitrile, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The material comprises Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 93% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the grain boundary resistance of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3InCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. A solid-state battery comprising the LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state battery. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.9 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm is provided. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The arsenic-free antimony content of 1 mol% to 4 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 0.7 mS/cm or more. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours is 75% or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2 mS/cm or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The oxygen substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A precursor of the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours is 80% or more.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.3 MPa or more. The binder content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability and cycle life of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6 material. The Al2O3 layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The Al2O3 layer of 500 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 50 nm to 3000 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The content of Li2O is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The solid electrolyte shows improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the content of Li2O is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more during cycling is described. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.3 MPa or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The LiF material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The LiF material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and production method thereof
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the electronic conductivity of the ion-conductive solid layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The critical current density is 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved interfacial resistance and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the silver additive is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by sputtering. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% over 100 cycles. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved moisture stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.3 V is provided. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The capacity retention of 90% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without fluoroethylene carbonate. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium yttrium chloride and to a method for producing the same. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The LiNbO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% over 100 cycles. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%.
