A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The binder content is 3 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved cycle life and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 45 wt% to 90 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 160 degrees C.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 60 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyacrylonitrile chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The plasticizer succinonitrile enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C. The polyacrylonitrile electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, succinonitrile, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 16:1.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Described is a lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. In the orthorhombic structure, erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved ionic conductivity and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, LLTO, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 10 MPa to 40 MPa, and the critical current density is 3 mA/cm2. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The suppression of void formation improves the sinterability and high-voltage stability during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer comprises solid electrolyte particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The solid content is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the solid electrolyte, and the layer shows improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Multilayer ceramic gas sensor element and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid state electrochemical sensor element with a built-in heater that keeps the ceramic at 300 degrees C. The sensor detects carbon dioxide with high selectivity and a response time of 5 seconds. The ceramic is yttria-stabilized zirconia and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 300 degrees C. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. The sensing electrode comprises lanthanum strontium manganite and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 300 degrees C. The sensor operating at 300 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for carbon dioxide.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium indium bromide ion-conductive solid with monoclinic structure for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium indium bromide ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 15 mol%. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1150 degrees C, and the resulting density is 96%. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The dopant tantalum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.1 to 0.45, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 88% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.06 <= v <= 0.75.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3YCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium yttrium chloride and to a method for producing the same. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium yttrium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm is provided. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 73% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The lithium battery is operated at 80 degrees C under a stack pressure of 600 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 600 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. The Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75.

assignee_std: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 5 nm to 300 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tantalum and sintered with Al2O3 is described. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. When v is 0.25, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 93% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 2 stacked cells
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 100 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by roll pressing and the release film is peeled. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 200 kPa. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The roll pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The resulting LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and LiNbO3 material. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which solid electrolyte particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The binder content is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 3 MPa and a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 16% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and LiF composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers, a porosity of 10%, a tensile strength of 3 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The method shortens the process and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C, and wherein the content of Li2O is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The lithium tungstate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more.

title: Niobium-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 94% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 91% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 91% or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 8.5 mS/cm. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The oxygen content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 2.2 mS/cm or more. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours is 80% or more.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiF, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 5 nm to 300 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 45% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which zirconium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium bromide framework. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6.

assignee_std: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a magnesium-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 2 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 1000 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The resulting Li3YCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 0.4 MPa to 10 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.2% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a solid-state lithium battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.15 or less. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.05 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in xylene with a rubber binder and a dispersant. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The warm isostatic pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 600 MPa. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The LLTO, LLZO, and LATP material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 50 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 200 kPa
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 200 MPa. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The cold isostatic pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 10% or less, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder.
