A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid shows improved ionic conductivity and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3PS4 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The 100 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyacrylonitrile; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which titanium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium bromide framework. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a silver additive. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more and a critical current density of 1.5 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the silver additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.2% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.25 <= x <= 1.05, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4. The additive content is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, the stack pressure is 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and the critical current density is 3 mA/cm2. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.5 wt% to 25 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more.

title: Solid oxide electrolysis cell and reversible fuel cell having a thin dense electrolyte
abstract: Provided is an oxygen-ion conducting ceramic electrolyte for a fuel cell that operates at 650 to 800 degrees C with a barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte and the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C. The thin 8 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.0 W/cm2. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite cell. The cathode comprises barium strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 650 to 800 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 95% or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 950 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, and wherein 0.01 <= v <= 0.7.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a tin substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. With germanium substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The total ionic conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.1 <= v <= 0.45, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3YCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3YCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The LiNbO3 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium erbium chloride ceramic ion conductor with monoclinic structure for lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The LiF, Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C.

title: Tin-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid in which tin substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The tensile strength is 0.6 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more.

assignee_std: DRIOSTUS ADVANCED MATERIALS TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on phosphate-based NASICON and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by atomic layer deposition. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 200 nm. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved interfacial resistance and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 1200 nm.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an oxygen substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The Li6PS5Cl and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The solid electrolyte provides improved electrochemical window and cycle life compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.05 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. An ionic conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.3 to 1.7. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The solid electrolyte provides improved electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 50 nm. The protective layer thickness is 20 nm to 100 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.3% or more. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl propionate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 50 micrometers. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The content of P2O5 is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of P2O5 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium yttrium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The electrode mixture of the solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by thermal evaporation followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The resulting LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The Li3N layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 7.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The lithium borate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the lithium secondary battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the moisture stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%, and wherein the content of Li2O is 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state battery using it. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium yttrium chloride and to a method for producing the same. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3InCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3YCl6. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability.
