The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 70% or more.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: Described is a combination of lithium difluorophosphate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. With 3 wt% of lithium difluorophosphate, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. The additive lithium difluorophosphate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 85% with the electrolyte. The stable passivation film formed by lithium difluorophosphate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The combination of lithium difluorophosphate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising lithium difluorophosphate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The lithium tungstate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Br6. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.6 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.9 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The oxidation potential is 5 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 87% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: A wet film of a solid electrolyte cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 15 micrometers. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the solid electrolyte, and the layer shows improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 30 wt% to 50 wt%.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The tin substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with an indium additive. Specific examples are Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more and a critical current density of 4 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 25 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF). The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3BO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The resulting Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and LiF material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more.

assignee_std: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the lithium secondary battery. A Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more and a critical current density of 4 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.5 wt% to 25 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3YCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li3YCl6. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. The arsenic-free antimony content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 0.7 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 55% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 2 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.2 MPa or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 10% or less.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The LiPON layer of 500 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the dendrite suppression and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 50 nm to 3000 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved sinterability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a zinc-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more and a critical current density of 3 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The Li6PS5Cl and LGPS material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The Li6PS5Cl and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the moisture stability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The LiPON layer of 200 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor element with a polyaniline layer and a carbon cathode layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a niobium solid electrolytic capacitor with a low equivalent series resistance and a high rated voltage. The capacitor withstands 105 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion. The niobium capacitor element is encapsulated in an epoxy resin with the anode lead and cathode terminal exposed. The solid electrolyte is the conductive polymer layer that serves as the true cathode of the capacitor. The polystyrene sulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 105 degrees C storage. The niobium anode body with the polymer cathode gives a volumetric efficiency higher than a liquid electrolyte capacitor.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor comprising a plurality of capacitor elements stacked and electrically connected in parallel, each capacitor element comprising a niobium anode body, a dielectric layer, and a conductive polymer layer, and a resin encapsulation, wherein the capacitor has a rated voltage of 6.3 V.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and zirconium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and LiF material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and LiF material. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the moisture stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which titanium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium chloride framework. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF). Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the solid-state battery. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF material. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material. Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. A Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more and a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO, Li3YCl6, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. An all-solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved dendrite suppression and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.8% or more.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers after calendering. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved interfacial resistance and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 32% or less, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 200 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The bilayer structure improves the cycle life and dendrite suppression compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The tin substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 65% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

assignee_std: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The critical current density is 1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium indium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The LiNbO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4. The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a ceramic ion conductor layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The low electronic conductivity of the LLZO, Li3PS4, and LiF material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The Al2O3 layer of 200 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life and ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 7.2 mS/cm or more.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing SiS2. A solid-state battery comprising the LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1.
