A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 420 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The binder content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life and electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 30% or less.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The silicon substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The low electronic conductivity of the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 80% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, LLZO, and LiF material. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1150 degrees C, and the resulting density is 94%. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.2 micrometers to 12 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 86% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.24 mS/cm or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.6 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5% after 100 cycles. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium indium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The resulting Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ion-conductive solid in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. In the orthorhombic structure, erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The LiF and Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. A precursor of the LiF and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The LLTO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.5 V. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNbO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium fluoride (LiF). The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 30 nm to 1800 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a ceramic ion conductor sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 15%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 250 micrometers, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 60% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which zinc is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 2 MPa. The suppression of void formation improves the dendrite suppression during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. A precursor of the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF). A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state battery. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer that has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 80 degrees C to 180 degrees C, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 50 mPa s to 2500 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The suppression of void formation improves the dendrite suppression during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more.

title: Surface mount solid electrolytic capacitor and method of reducing leakage current
abstract: A hybrid capacitor combining a conductive polymer layer and an electrolytic solution is described. The solid electrolyte of the capacitor is formed from a conductive polymer dispersion. The polyaniline is doped with p-toluenesulfonate and has a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm in the dispersion. The tantalum anode body with the polymer cathode gives a volumetric efficiency higher than a liquid electrolyte capacitor. A carbon layer and a silver paste layer are formed on the polyaniline layer to serve as the cathode lead-out. A capacitance of 220 microfarads is obtained in a case size of 7.3 mm by 4.3 mm. The hybrid structure improves the self-healing of the dielectric film on the tantalum anode.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising: anodizing a porous tantalum anode body to form a dielectric oxide film; impregnating the anode body with a dispersion of polyaniline particles having a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm; drying the dispersion to form a conductive polymer layer; and forming a carbon layer and a silver layer on the conductive polymer layer.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. An all-solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3InCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The ion-conductive solid shows improved electrochemical window and moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the content of LiI is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The content of Li2O is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A precursor of the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of Li2O is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 2 mA/cm2. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. An all-solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3InCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.6 MPa or more. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers, a porosity of 8%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The method shortens the process and improves the ionic conductivity and sheet formability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 400 micrometers, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 160 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. When z is 0.3, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. The Li3InCl6 and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7.

title: Anode-supported solid oxide fuel cell having a thin samarium-doped ceria electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 500 to 650 degrees C. The samarium-doped ceria electrolyte of 96% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 500 to 650 degrees C. The solid electrolyte of samarium-doped ceria is a dense ceramic of 96% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the samarium-doped ceria electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments. The stack shows stable operation over 100 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 500 to 650 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 500 to 650 degrees C.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The cold isostatic pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The structure with the nickel-plated copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the content of Li2O is 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polycarbonate. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polycarbonate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polycarbonate; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%, and wherein the content of LiI is 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more is described. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 80% or more. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO, LATP, and LLZO material. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 70% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.12 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. The Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state lithium battery using it. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 55% or more.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO solid electrolyte stable above 5 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1.
