The content of SiS2 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 420 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The protective layer thickness is 200 nm to 1000 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.8% or more. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance and electrochemical window of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 50 nm to 3000 nm.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a solid electrolyte is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The LATP, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent butyl butyrate. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.8 mS/cm or more.

assignee_std: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a Li3N inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% after 100 cycles. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of Li2O is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The silicon content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 0.7 mS/cm or more. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 55% or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 material. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 91% or more after sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the cycle life and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 86% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1000 degrees C to 1350 degrees C, and wherein 0.21 <= v <= 0.9.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3InCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The indium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more and a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mA/cm2 or more.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 500 kPa
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and a conductive agent.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 7.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.35 <= y/a <= 0.65.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The content of LiI is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm or more. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the moisture stability is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The solid electrolyte provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. The material comprises Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved ionic conductivity and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A solid-state battery comprising the LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3). In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.5 V. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF, Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The Li2ZrO3 and LATP material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. The mixed halogen substitution improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity of the all-solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the grain boundary resistance are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which titanium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium chloride framework. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tungsten stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1100 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a relative density of 97%. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The method gives reproducible densification and improved sinterability at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 89% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%, and wherein 0.01 <= v <= 0.7.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The method gives reproducible densification and improved sinterability at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 91% or more.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. The oxygen content of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 2.2 mS/cm or more. The oxygen substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Br6 and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of indium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.5 V. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, InBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. The low electronic conductivity of the LiF, Li3YCl6, and LiNbO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The tin content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 0.7 mS/cm or more. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a tin substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 65% or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 93% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The sintered body has a relative density of 96%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.1 <= v <= 0.45, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ion-conductive solid. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li3InCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% after 100 cycles. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Sintering at 1200 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved moisture stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 84% or more, and wherein 0.11 <= v <= 0.8, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more.

title: lithium sulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. Polysulfide dissolution from the lithium sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 80% at 25 degrees C. The initial capacity of 600 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the lithium sulfide cathode. The carbon coating on the lithium sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The cathode delivering 600 mAh/g is assembled into a lithium battery with a lithium metal foil.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising lithium sulfide, graphene, and carboxymethyl cellulose, wherein a loading of the lithium sulfide is 5 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The Li3PS4 and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The Li3N layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 30% or less is provided. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The Li6PS5Cl and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The binder content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3InCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on phosphate-based NASICON and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.5 V. The low electronic conductivity of the LLTO, LLZO, and LATP material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. In the trigonal structure, scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and method for preparing the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by solution casting followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved high-voltage stability and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 material. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1.
