A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of indium and zirconium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF). The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 1.47 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved moisture stability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 80 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.2 to 0.45, and a method for producing the same are provided. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 5 nm to 300 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the lithium secondary battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. After heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The binder content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 160 degrees C.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which silver is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% to suppress dendrites. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The silver additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The additive content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, the stack pressure is 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and the critical current density is 1 mA/cm2. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The LiF and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which zirconium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The low electronic conductivity of the LiF and Li3InCl6 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. An ionic conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.1 to 1.5. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein 0.9 <= a <= 1.7.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa with a zinc additive. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. With the additive in an amount of 5 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7%. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.5 wt% to 25 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 40 cycles or more.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.3 MPa or more. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The sheet thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, the porosity is 20% or less, and the conductivity is 1.4 mS/cm or more. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A precursor of the LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 250 micrometers, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 40% or less.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sheet thickness is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, the porosity is 30% or less, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 60% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 400 micrometers.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 80 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and LLZO material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.075 or less. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.05 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 6 mS/cm. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.75.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in ethyl acetate at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a ceramic ion conductor sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The binder content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4, LATP, and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 180 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 0.9 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl acetate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 8%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved interfacial resistance and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 250 micrometers.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an oxygen substitution amount of 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%.

title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The resulting Li3YCl6 and LiF material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1.5 mA/cm2. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. In the trigonal structure, scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A precursor of the Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state battery. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The content of Li2O is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours, and wherein the content of Li2O is 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. A solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tungsten-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 94% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 94% or more after sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.15 to 0.5, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the sinterability of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.11 <= v <= 0.8, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 0.5 micrometers to 30 micrometers.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: A wet film of a ceramic ion conductor cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The resulting LATP, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent butyl butyrate. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A lithium secondary battery using the layer shows improved sheet formability and a thin electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 20 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Specific examples are Li3YCl6. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A precursor of the Li7P3S11, LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 1 wt%. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 40 wt%.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobium tantalum oxide formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3InCl6. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a styrene-butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C in an oven. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A lithium secondary battery using the layer shows improved ionic conductivity and a thin electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 15 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 300 mPa s to 15000 mPa s.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3YCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium zirconate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3InCl6. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. The lithium fluoride additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 1 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 200 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The suppression of void formation improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 40 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2 MPa to 50 MPa.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer that has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent heptane. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 100 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 2 stacked cells
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 500 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder.
