A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 87% or more. The Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 32% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a magnesium additive. The resulting Li7P3S11 and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and LLZO material. The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more and a critical current density of 3 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tungsten stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 900 degrees C to 1250 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers.

title: Perovskite-type lithium lanthanum titanate solid electrolyte with a lithium zirconate surface region stable against oxidation and reduction
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte comprises grains of a perovskite-type lithium lanthanum titanate represented by Li(3x)La(2/3-x)TiO3, wherein 0.08 <= x <= 0.13, and a surface region of lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) having a thickness of 5 nm to 40 nm formed on the grains by a zirconium alkoxide treatment and an oxygen anneal at 600 degrees C to 750 degrees C. The surface region suppresses both the oxidative decomposition of the titanate above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ and the reduction of titanium below 1.7 V, so that the electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends from 1.0 V to 5.2 V. A sintered body of the treated grains has a relative density of 94% or more and a grain boundary resistance of 30% or less of the total resistance, and shows a total ionic conductivity of 0.25 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A lithium borosilicate glass ceramic added in an amount of 2 wt% to 5 wt% fills the grain boundaries and further lowers the grain boundary resistance. The solid electrolyte can be used with a lithium metal anode when a lithium fluoride interface layer is interposed, and with a high-voltage positive electrode charged to 4.8 V, giving a cell with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte comprising: grains of a perovskite-type lithium lanthanum titanate represented by Li(3x)La(2/3-x)TiO3, wherein 0.08 <= x <= 0.13; and a surface region comprising Li2ZrO3 formed on the grains and having a thickness of 5 nm to 40 nm, wherein an electrochemical window of the oxide solid electrolyte measured by cyclic voltammetry at 0.1 mV/s on a blocking electrode extends from 1.0 V to 5.2 V versus Li/Li+.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using ethyl propionate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The reaction at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and moisture stability and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an oxygen substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The oxide particles have a core of the NASICON-type LATP phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 90%. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium fluoride (LiF). Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more during cycling is described. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 100 MPa. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 80 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The Al2O3 layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The protective layer thickness is 20 nm to 100 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.3% or more. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 5 nm to 300 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl propionate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. Specific examples are Li3InCl6. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.35 <= y/a <= 0.65, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of indium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which titanium is substituted for part of the indium in a lithium indium bromide framework. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. When z is 0.3, the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. In the trigonal structure, indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LATP and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers, a porosity of 15%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.3 MPa or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 60% or less, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 160 degrees C.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1230 degrees C, and the resulting density is 92%. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1030 degrees C to 1380 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.5 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein 0.06 <= v <= 0.75.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A precursor of the LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 45% or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 0.84 mS/cm or more. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% after 100 cycles. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium metal layer, a ceramic ion conductor layer, and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The cell shows no short circuit for 300 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 10 MPa. The method prevents short circuit and improves the ionic conductivity without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium indium chloride and to a method for producing the same. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the solid-state lithium battery. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. A solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. A lithium battery pack comprising 8 modules of the stacked cells is also described.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.3 to 0.75. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and the critical current density is 3 mA/cm2. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ion-conductive solid layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium metal layer, a ceramic ion conductor layer, and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The method prevents short circuit and improves the ionic conductivity without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 0.4 MPa to 10 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.5 wt% to 25 wt%.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in ethyl acetate at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more and a critical current density of 3 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The magnesium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2 MPa to 50 MPa.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 50 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium scandium bromide ceramic ion conductor with trigonal structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 250 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with aluminum and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.24 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 89% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 30% to 65% by X-ray diffraction. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6. The bilayer structure improves the dendrite suppression compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 1200 nm.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. The Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.5 V
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.35 mS/cm or more. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the sinterability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6 for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which zirconium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium bromide framework. The LiF and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF and LiNbO3 material. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting solid electrolyte film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The binder content is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 3 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LATP material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material.
