A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the content of Li2O is 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with a zinc additive. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The critical current density is 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The tin substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 2 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with an indium additive. The Li3YCl6 and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The critical current density is 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state lithium battery using it. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%, and wherein the content of LiI is 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium indium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The Li3InCl6, LiNbO3, and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6, LiNbO3, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 32 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a ceramic ion conductor sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. A sheet of 80 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the sheet formability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 55% or more.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The LiF composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the dendrite suppression is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%, and wherein the content of LiI is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The silicon substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.8.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The binder content is 2 wt%, the drying temperature is 60 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved sheet formability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 75 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 20 degrees C to 120 degrees C.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 0.84 mS/cm or more. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The method shortens the process and improves the electrochemical window and interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ion-conductive solid in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The protective layer thickness is 40 nm to 200 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.8% or more. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.4 to 1.8. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The ceramic ion conductor provides improved cycle life and moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Gallium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The low electronic conductivity of the Li2ZrO3, LLZO, and LATP material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, LLZO, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1100 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a relative density of 96%. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 900 degrees C to 1250 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 0 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state battery is described. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3YCl6. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state battery. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3YCl6 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 1 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%, and wherein 0.31 <= v <= 1.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The resulting Li2ZrO3 and LiF material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 2 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar aluminum current collectors. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The current collector of aluminum is used in a lithium battery with a 50 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 4.5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO, LATP, and LLTO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The LLZO, LATP, and LLTO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.12 mS/cm or more.

assignee_std: DRIOSTUS ADVANCED MATERIALS TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and capacitor using the same
abstract: A hybrid capacitor combining a conductive polymer layer and an electrolytic solution is described. A re-formation step after polymer formation repairs defects in the dielectric film and reduces the leakage current. The conductive polymer layer contains a polyhydric alcohol as an additive that improves the coverage on the dielectric. The aluminum anode body with the polymer cathode gives a volumetric efficiency higher than a liquid electrolyte capacitor. The equivalent series resistance is 5 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less. The capacitor rated at 16 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage. A solid electrolyte of polyaniline replaces the liquid electrolyte of a conventional electrolytic capacitor.
first_claim: 1. A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising polyaniline particles doped with polystyrene sulfonate, a polyhydric alcohol, and water, wherein the particles have a median diameter of 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The LATP material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A sheet of 30 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.3 MPa or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by uniaxial pressing. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3YCl6. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a beta-Li3PS4 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The LiF, Li3YCl6, and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The LiF, Li3YCl6, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ceramic ion conductor in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, LLTO, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The LLZO, LiF, and Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The LLZO, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The LiF layer of 100 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved dendrite suppression and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more.

assignee_std: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. An ionic conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.3 to 1.7. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ion-conductive solid. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 2 MPa. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.8% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP material. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The method gives reproducible densification and improved ionic conductivity at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.1 <= v <= 0.45, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 92% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.42 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ceramic ion conductor in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1.
