A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 97% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The dopant tantalum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 89% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 3 mol% to 23 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1030 degrees C to 1380 degrees C.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in acetonitrile at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 80% after humid exposure. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the grain boundary resistance are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours is 70% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The resulting LiNbO3 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. The LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The resulting Li3PS4 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 90%. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the grain boundary resistance in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 25 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The Li6PS5Cl and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the high-voltage stability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 30% to 65% by X-ray diffraction. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sheet formability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. The oxygen content of 1 mol% to 4 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 55% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. With tin substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 180 degrees C.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The LiF and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 30 nm to 1800 nm.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The Li2ZrO3 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. The LLTO, LATP, and LLZO material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1150 degrees C, and the resulting density is 96%. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the solid-state battery. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 93% or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. The content of P2O5 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.8 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. The solid electrolyte shows improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for producing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The LGPS and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The ion-conductive solid shows improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.75.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The low electronic conductivity of the LLZO material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.5 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 86% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 3 mol% to 23 mol%.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The laminate of 4 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 4 cells and a case is also provided. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte
abstract: Provided is an oxygen-ion conducting ceramic electrolyte for a fuel cell that operates at 700 to 850 degrees C with a lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The solid electrolyte layer of yttria-stabilized zirconia conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 700 to 850 degrees C. The cell operates at 700 to 850 degrees C with a power density of 0.8 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 200 cycles. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the yttria-stabilized zirconia cell. The lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 700 to 850 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 3 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium erbium chloride ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ion-conductive solid in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1 <= a <= 1.8.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. Sintering at 1150 degrees C with a lithium excess of 5 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The low grain boundary resistance results in improved cycle life compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.16 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 0 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 1 micrometers to 60 micrometers.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. The Li3PS4 and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 15 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 75 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein 0.9 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.65.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which magnesium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% to suppress dendrites. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF). The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1 mA/cm2. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The Li3InCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The lithium yttrium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in ethyl acetate at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.6 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Germanium-substituted NASICON-type LATP solid electrolyte stable above 4.5 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The oxide particles have a core of the NASICON-type LATP phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 87% or more.

title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The protective layer thickness is 120 nm to 600 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. The material comprises Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 30 nm to 1800 nm.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 0.84 mS/cm or more. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2WO4 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99% and no dendrite penetration is observed. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1.
