The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 77% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 3.9 V or more.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The LiF material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more.

title: Hafnium-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid stable above 5 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 87% or more. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved sinterability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 77% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 50 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the indium in a lithium indium chloride framework. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiF and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved ionic conductivity and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with tantalum and sintered with Li2CO3 is described. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1200 degrees C, and the resulting density is 95%. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 92% or more, and wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LiF material. Specific examples are Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The material comprises Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The bilayer structure improves the cycle life compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 5 nm to 300 nm.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.3 V is provided. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 92% of its capacity after 500 cycles. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The additive 1,3-propane sultone reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive 1,3-propane sultone decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. With tin substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The low electronic conductivity of the Li2ZrO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which solid electrolyte particles are dispersed in butyl butyrate with a rubber binder and a dispersant. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The Li3YCl6 and LiF material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent butyl butyrate. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The Li3YCl6 and LiF composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the moisture stability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of an ion-conductive solid with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.6 MPa or more. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The resulting Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 30% or less.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 70% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ion-conductive solid provides improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The low electronic conductivity of the LLZO and Li7P3S11 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 55% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 200 nm. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.8% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The resulting Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The viscosity of 1000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the interfacial resistance and sheet formability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours.

title: Lithium nitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The Li3PS4 and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The Li3N layer of 50 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. The LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The tin substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life and moisture stability compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein 0.2 <= y/a <= 0.5.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The resulting LiF material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 250 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF). The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of erbium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.3 to 0.55, and a method for producing the same are provided. The Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm. The Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.12 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. An H2S generation of 4 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and Li7P3S11 material. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and moisture stability and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a Li3N inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiF, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The Li3N layer of 200 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 1200 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%, and wherein the content of Li2O is 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and production method thereof
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 5.2 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The LLZO, Li2ZrO3, and LLTO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. The germanium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a lithium fluoride-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 300 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The suppression of void formation improves the dendrite suppression during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on phosphate-based NASICON and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%, and wherein the content of LiI is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium zirconate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3 material. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which lithium fluoride is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more and a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The lithium fluoride additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved cycle life and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more.

title: Tin-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 87% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. Specific examples are Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5% after 100 cycles. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and ionic conductivity and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.
