assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The content of SiS2 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The Li2ZrO3 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The content of LiI is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C.

title: Multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor with improved heat resistance at 125 degrees C
abstract: A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and a capacitor using the dispersion are provided. The niobium anode body with the polymer cathode gives a volumetric efficiency higher than a liquid electrolyte capacitor. The polystyrene sulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 125 degrees C storage. The dielectric oxide film is formed by anodizing the niobium anode body in a phosphoric acid solution at a formation voltage of 2 to 4 times the rated voltage. A carbon layer and a silver paste layer are formed on the polypyrrole layer to serve as the cathode lead-out. The capacitor withstands 125 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less.
first_claim: 1. A solid electrolytic capacitor comprising: an anode body comprising a porous sintered body of niobium; a dielectric layer formed on a surface of the anode body; a conductive polymer layer disposed on the dielectric layer and comprising polypyrrole doped with polystyrene sulfonate; and a cathode layer comprising carbon and silver disposed on the conductive polymer layer, wherein an equivalent series resistance of the capacitor at 100 kHz is 5 milliohms or less.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 73% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 50 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. In the trigonal structure, scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. The median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 80 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a aluminum current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 2 stacked cells. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering an aluminum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 93% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the interfacial resistance of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. The lithium fluoride additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 2 MPa. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%.

title: Germanium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 2 mol% to 40 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 3.9 V or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to a solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.045 or less. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm and a relative density of 96%. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 88% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1000 degrees C to 1350 degrees C.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The protective layer thickness is 20 nm to 100 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life and dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more and a conductivity of 0.35 mS/cm or more. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. The oxygen substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.045 or less. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein 0.25 <= x <= 1.05, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. In the orthorhombic structure, indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 70% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The binder content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP, Li3PS4, and LLZO material. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.2 MPa or more.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer comprises ion-conductive solid particles, a polyisobutylene binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sinterability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 50 mPa s to 2500 mPa s, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LATP material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The tin substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium yttrium chloride and to a method for producing the same. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The resulting LiNbO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. The resulting Li7P3S11 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The material comprises Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours is 70% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 0.9 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 50 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The wet film is dried at 100 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and beta-Li3PS4. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 200 mPa s to 10000 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 15 wt% to 60 wt%.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy for lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid provides improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 7.2 mS/cm or more.
